translations.text: Moses began to declare this law and said:
At that time I said to you, ‘I cannot bear you alone.’
How can I alone bear your trouble, your affairs, and your disputes?

Where, then, are we to go up? Your brothers discouraged your hearts and told you, ‘The people are great and numerous, and stronger than we are. Their cities are large, with fortifications reaching up to heaven. We also saw the children of giants there.’
The Lord was angry with me also because of you, and he told me, ‘You too shall not enter there.’
But you turned back and traveled into the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea.
The Amorites who lived on that mountain came out to meet you, fell upon you, pursued you, and stung you like bees. They struck you down from Seir to Hormah.
Command the people and tell them, ‘Look, you are passing through the territory of your brothers, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir, and they will be very afraid of you.’
The Emim formerly lived in it, a very great people, strong like those in [?].
And when all those fighting men had fallen and died from among the people,
Sell me food for my gold, so that I may eat, and sell me water for my gold, so that I may drink. I will only pass through on foot.
Except for their livestock, which we took as spoil for ourselves; and we plundered the cities we captured.
But your wives and your children—and I know that you have many livestock—shall remain in your cities, which I gave you,

until the Lord our God gives your brothers rest as he has given you, and they too possess the land that the Lord our God is giving them beyond the Jordan. Then all of you shall return to your inheritance, which I gave you.
At that time I also commanded Joshua and told him, ‘Your eyes have seen everything the Lord did to these two kings. The Lord will do the same to every kingdom into which you go.’

O Lord God, you have begun to show your servant your strength and your power, the strength of your hand and the greatness of your arm. What god is there in heaven or on earth who does what you have done?
Do not add to the word that I command you today, and do not take anything away from it, so that you may keep all the commandments of the Lord your God.
in the likeness of any animal on the earth, or in the likeness of any winged bird that flies beneath heaven;
But the Lord took you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, so that you would be his own people, as you are to this day.
The Lord will scatter you among all the nations, and you will be left few in number among the nations into which the Lord brings you.
Know today that the Lord God is the Lord in heaven above and on earth below, and there is no other besides him.
Bezer in the wilderness, in the open country, for Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead for Gad; and Golan in Bashan for Manasseh.
They took possession of his land and the land of Og, king of Bashan—the two kings of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise.
Moses called all Israel and said to them, ‘Listen, Israel, to all the statutes and judgments that I speak in your hearing today, on this day. Learn to carry them out and keep them.’

The seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God. On it you shall not do any of your work, neither you nor your son nor your daughter nor your male servant nor your female servant nor your ox nor your donkey nor any of your livestock nor the foreigner within your gates, so that your male servant and your female servant may rest as you do.
Do not go to another man's wife. Do not kill anyone. Do not steal. Do not be a false witness against your neighbor. Do not falsify testimony.

These are the words the Lord spoke to your entire assembly on the mountain, from the midst of fire, darkness, storm, and thick cloud, with a loud voice. He added nothing more. He wrote them on two stone tablets, and the Lord gave them to me.
For what mortal has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of fire, as we have, and remained alive?
But you, stand beside me. I will tell you all my commandments, statutes, and laws, which you are to teach them so that they may follow them in the land I am giving them as their inheritance.
Along the whole path that the Lord your God commanded you to follow, so that things may go well for you, that you may have rest, and that your days may be long in the land you will inherit.
Do not follow other gods, the gods of the nations around you.
Do not put the Lord your God to the test as you tested him on the day of testing.
Do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God, so that things may go well for you and you may enter and inherit the blessed land that the Lord swore to your fathers.
The Lord sent great and terrible signs and wonders against Egypt, against Pharaoh, and against his household, before our eyes.
For he will turn your son away from me, and your son will worship other gods. The Lord's anger will burn against you, and he will quickly destroy you.
He will repay those who hate him to their faces and destroy them. He will not delay the destruction of those who hate him, but will confront them directly.
Keep all his commandments, statutes, and laws that I command you today, and carry them out.
Do not bring an unclean thing into your house and become accursed like it. Regard it as utterly unclean and utterly detest it, for it is accursed.
Keep all the commandments of the Lord your God, walking in his ways and fearing him.
He fed you in the wilderness with manna, which your fathers did not know, to afflict you and test you, and to do good to you in your later days.
The Lord gave me two stone tablets inscribed with the finger of the Lord. On them were written all the words the Lord spoke to us on the mountain on the day you assembled.

And when the Lord sent you from Kadesh-barnea and said to you, "Go up and take possession of the land I am giving you," you rebelled against the word of the Lord your God. You did not trust him or listen to his voice.
You have been rebellious against the Lord from the day he became known to you.

I prayed to the Lord and said, "Lord, King of the gods, do not destroy your people, your own portion, whom you redeemed by your great power and brought out of Egypt by your great power, your strong hand, and your uplifted arm."
I will write on these tablets all the words that were on the earlier tablets you broke. Put them in the ark.
I stayed on the mountain for forty days and forty nights. The Lord listened to me during those days too, and the Lord spared you and did not destroy you.
Look, heaven, the heaven of heavens, the earth, and everything in it belong to the Lord your God.
Fear the Lord your God, worship him alone, follow him, and swear by his name.
Love the Lord your God and keep his law, statutes, commandments, and judgments throughout all the days of your life.
So that your days may be long in the land that the Lord swore to give to your fathers and their descendants after them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And the Lord will become angry with you and shut the sky, so that no rain comes and the earth does not yield its fruit, and you will quickly perish from the blessed land that the Lord has given you.
And if you faithfully obey every commandment that I give you today, carrying them out, loving the Lord your God, walking in all his ways, and following him;
And you must not do this to the Lord your God.
And when the Lord your God destroys before you the nations whose land you are entering to possess, and you dispossess them and live in their land;
And his sign or wonder that he told you about comes to pass, while he says, “Come, let us go and worship gods that you do not know”;
Follow the Lord your God, fear him, keep his commandments, listen to his voice, and take refuge in him.

Gather all its goods into its streets and burn the city with fire, together with all its goods. Treat the whole city in this way before the Lord your God. No one shall ever live in it, and it shall not be rebuilt.
And this is what you may eat from the water: eat anything that has fins and scales.
But do not eat anything that has no fins and scales; it is unclean for you.
And these are the birds you must not eat: the eagle, the vulture, and the sea eagle;
And if there is someone impoverished among your brothers in one of your towns that the Lord your God has given you, do not turn your heart away or close your hand against giving to your brother.
Instead, open your hand wide and give your brother what he asks of you, from what he asks of you.
And remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt and that the Lord your God redeemed you from there. For this reason I command you to do this.

Do not eat leavened bread with it. For seven days eat unleavened bread with it, the bread of suffering, because you came out of Egypt in haste, so that you may remember the day you came out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life.

Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Lord your God in the place that the Lord your God has chosen: at the festival of the law of Hallelujah, at the festival of the Sabbath, and at the festival of Booths. Do not come before the Lord your God empty-handed.

And if a matter of judgment is too difficult for you, between blood and blood, between cleanness and purification, or between injury and injury—matters of judgment within your towns—you shall rise and go up to the place that the Lord your God has chosen for his name to be named there.
And it shall remain with him, and he shall read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn the way of the Lord his God, keep all his commandments, and carry out his judgments;
And he shall serve in the name of the Lord his God, like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the Lord.
For those nations that you are dispossessing practice divination and listen to oracles, but it is not to be so with you.
And others shall hear and be afraid, and shall not again do this evil thing among you.
And you shall show him no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, and foot for foot.

And the officers shall say to the people, “If there is a man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it, let him go and return to his house, so that he does not die in battle and another man dedicate his house.”
And the elders of that city shall bring the heifer to a rugged valley that has not been plowed or sown, and there in the valley they shall cut the heifer’s tendons.
Forgive your people Israel, Lord, whom you redeemed from the land of Egypt, so that guilt for taking a life may not rest upon your people Israel. And they will be forgiven for that life.
Afterward, if you do not want her, you shall let her go free. You must not sell her for gold or deal treacherously with her, since you married her.
If a man has a rebellious and insolent son who does not obey his father or his mother, and they discipline him but he does not listen to them;
If you see your neighbor’s donkey or his ox fallen on the road, do not ignore them. Help him lift it up.
If you come upon a bird’s brood before you on the road, in any tree or on the ground, whether chicks or eggs, do not take the mother with her young.
Do not speak of peace or well-being for them throughout all your days, forever.
Take a wooden implement with you in your belt. When you sit down, dig a hole, then get up and cover your excrement.
Do not bring the earnings of prostitution or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord your God for any vow, for both are unclean before the Lord your God.
Do not take a mill or its upper millstone as a pledge, for it is a means of sustaining life, and it must not be taken as a pledge.
If there is a dispute between people and they come to court to have their case judged, the judges shall acquit the one who is right and condemn the one who is wrong;
Do not keep for yourself a small measure and a large measure.
You shall say before the Lord your God, “My father left Syria and went down to Egypt. He lived there when they were few in number, and there he became a great nation, very populous and numerous.”
For the Lord has chosen you today to be his own people, as he said, so that you may keep all his commandments;
You shall build an altar to the Lord your God with stones that have not been hewn.
You shall offer sacrifices of well-being upon them. Eat and be satisfied there, and rejoice before the Lord your God.
Moses and the priests said to the Levites and to all Israel, “Be silent and listen, Israel. On this day you have become the people of the Lord your God.”
Cursed be anyone who dishonors his father and his mother. And all the people shall say, “Amen and amen.”
You will have sons and daughters, but they will not be left to you, for they will be taken away and led into captivity.
It will be a sign and a wonder upon you and upon your descendants forever.
Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and a glad heart when you had an abundance of everything.
The Lord will bring against you a nation from far away, from the ends of the earth, like an eagle swooping down—a nation whose speech you do not understand;
A nation with a fierce face, which does not respect the elderly or show mercy to the young;
The woman among you who is delicate and weak, who [?] her feet to walk on the ground because she is delicate and weak, will look begrudgingly at the husband in her embrace, her son, and her daughter.
If you do not obey and carry out all the words of this law written in this book, so that you fear this honored and glorious name, that of the Lord your God.
He will bring back upon them all those evil diseases of Egypt which you did not fear (from which you did not fear) when confronted with them, and they will cling to you.
The Lord will bring upon you every disease and every plague that is not written in this book of the law, until he destroys you and you are wiped out.
So that he may make you his people and may himself be your God, as he swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

Let there be no man or woman, people or tribe, or anyone among you whose heart turns away from the Lord your God and who goes to worship these gods of the nations. Let there be no evil root among you that sprouts and bears poison and bitterness.

The Lord will not be willing to forgive him. Instead, at that time the Lord’s anger and jealousy will burn against that man, and every curse of this covenant written in this book of the law will pursue him. The Lord will erase his name from under heaven.

The later generation, your children who rise up after you, and the foreigner who comes from a distant land will speak when they see the plagues of that land and the diseases that the Lord has sent upon it;

For I will bring them into the blessed land that I swore to their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey. When they have eaten and are satisfied, they will grow fat and turn to other gods and worship them. They will provoke me and abandon my covenant.
Moses commanded Joshua and said to him, “Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the children of Israel into the land that the Lord swore to their fathers, and he will be with you.”
For I know your rebelliousness and your stubborn neck. Even while I am still alive today, you have rebelled against the Lord. How much more will you do so after my death!
For the Lord will judge his people and plead the cause of his servants, because he sees that they have wasted away and perished and have been abandoned where they are.

Let all the heavens rejoice together, and let all the angels of God bow down to him. Let the nations rejoice with their peoples, and let all the children of God say, “He is mighty!” For he will avenge the blood of his children. He will take vengeance and repay his adversaries with vengeance, and he will repay those who hate him. The Lord will cleanse the land for his people.
And when Moses had finished speaking to all Israel;
Die on the mountain that you ascend there, and join your people, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and joined his people.
This is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the children of Israel before he died.
He said, “The Lord came from Sinai and also appeared in Seir. He rested on Mount Paran with the myriads of Kadesh, those at his right, his angels, and those with him.”
Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died, and his eyes had neither grown dim nor deteriorated.
